posts.author: jean
posts.content_md:
I remember an old post about water in alcohol. Someone (sorry, I don't remember who), put silica gel in alcohol. The silica gel absorb water and you just need to filter. Be careful after this operation, place silica gel in a place with a strong air flow (outside preferably) because alcohol vapor can be harmful.

Silica gel can even be regenerated. Placing it in a oven and warm to 120°C so the water in can evaporate.

Myabe this technique can be used with 90% alcohol to get 95% or even 99% alcohol. What do you think ?

I seem to recall this coming up before, and there seemed to be a problem with distilling beyond the point where the water/alcohol mixture was an azeotrope ([http://www.solvent--recycling.com/azeotrope_1.htm](http://www.solvent--recycling.com/azeotrope_1.htm))

Beyond the azeotrope limit, more extreme measures are needed to remove the water.

posts.author: meekan01
posts.content_md:
4 liters for $25, lab grade absolute ethanol (<0.5% water) from vwr.com. Contains 5% methanol.

In case anyone is entertained by knowing such things, the postdoc in my lab told me how ethanol is made more than 95% pure. Basically, when you're trying to distill normally, the ethanol binds weakly to water in that 19-1 ratio and carries it along the distallation tube. In order to get it more pure, they used to put in Benzene, which attracts the water more, and then pull off the benzene with the remaining water. It's pretty cool.

I'm pretty sure that they don't do it with Benzene anymore, but I'm pretty sure they still use the same basic kind of idea- you mix in another chemical that has a greater tendancy to stick to the water =)

Cheers,
